searchText: Hi. After reading adietrichs's EIP-1559 txpool documentation, I came up with an algorithm that is faster than naive sorting every block in an EIP-1559 txpool. The fast algorithm can reduce the computational complexity of sorting from `O(n log n)` to `O(k log n)`. `n` is the number of transactions in a txpool, and `k` is the number of transactions where the miner bribe varies with basefee. If the change in basefee is small, then `k` is small compared to `n`. I've already implemented the prototype in C++. https://github.com/minaminao/eip1559txpool Also, I've tested it with a few parameters in my local environment, and it speeds up transaction selection by a factor of 20-50 without changing fees earned. Is there a need for this algorithm? I heard that Geth sorts transactions every block, so I doubt it is necessary. If there is a demand for this algorithm, I will write a detailed explanation of the algorithm and continue implementing it. Do you happen to have a human readable description of the strategy somewhere? For those of us who have purposefully forgotten how to read/write C++. 😬 Thank you for the response. I implemented the algorithm directly, so I'm writing the description now 🙂 Also, I'm good at algorithms, but I'm not an expert on ethereum clients, so I wanted to proceed based on reactions. The reason I wrote the algorithm in C++ is that it uses self-balancing binary search trees (SBST), but Python does not have SBST in the standard library. Before writing the explanation, I wanted to know if we need to speed up the computational complexity of sorting from `O(n log n)` to `O(k log n)`. Fork is firmed in January does it includes 1559 <@!748641831331561532> no, it doesn't. Nor is Berlin scheduled yet 😅 cc: <@!415548822983278593> 😄 <@!370136219927052298> re: > Is there a need for this algorithm? I heard that Geth sorts transactions every block, so I doubt it is necessary. If there is a demand for this algorithm, I will write a detailed explanation of the algorithm and continue implementing it. There is! I think if we can improve tx pool behavior via 1559, rather than make it worse, that's a great outcome! I think the SBST method can be applied to the current Geth txpool (not EIP-1559). I'm wondering why Geth sorts transactions by O(n log n) every block without using SBST. Anyway, I will write an explanation! Thank you! 1559 is against blockchain economy in current scenario .
